root_cause.text: The idxd driver’s event-log teardown path in `idxd_device_evl_free()` wrongly gated deallocation on the hardware `GENCFG.evl_en` register bit, so after device reset cleared the register to zero the allocated `idxd->evl` memory was never freed, causing a leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says “During the device remove process, the device is reset, causing the configuration registers to go back to their default state, which is zero” and “the driver is checking if the event log support was enabled before deallocating, it will fail if a reset happened before”; the diff removes `gencfg.bits = ioread32(...); if (!gencfg.evl_en) return;`, leaving only the `idxd->evl` validity check before freeing.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The idxd driver’s event-log teardown path in `idxd_device_evl_free()` wrongly gated deallocation on the hardware `GENCFG.evl_en` register bit, so after device reset cleared the register to zero the allocated `idxd->evl` memory was never freed, causing a leak.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message says “During the device remove process, the device is reset, causing the configuration registers to go back to their default state, which is zero” and “the driver is checking if the event log support was enabled before deallocating, it will fail if a reset happened before”; the diff removes `gencfg.bits = ioread32(...); if (!gencfg.evl_en) return;`, leaving only the `idxd->evl` validity check before freeing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always clear the EVL enable bit during device cleanup instead of skipping the update when it appears disabled.
intent_record.what: The function `idxd_device_evl_free()` no longer reads `IDXD_GENCFG_OFFSET` and checks `gencfg.evl_en` before continuing. The early return based on `!gencfg.evl_en` was removed, so the code now always acquires `evl->lock`, clears `gencfg.evl_en`, and writes the updated value back to the device register when `evl` is present.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the EVL cleanup path will now proceed even if the hardware configuration bit was not already set. This prevents the function from skipping the register update and ensures the EVL enable bit is explicitly cleared during device free, making cleanup more deterministic.

grouping_result.intent: Always clear the EVL enable bit during device cleanup instead of skipping the update when it appears disabled.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets EVL teardown/cleanup behavior in the idxd driver and corrects logic around the EVL enable bit, which is directly related to the leak caused by gating cleanup on GENCFG.evl_en being cleared after reset.

candidates.rationale: This early return wrongly skips EVL teardown when the hardware enable bit is already cleared, which matches the root cause: after reset the bit is zero, so cleanup never proceeds and the allocated event-log memory is leaked.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return gates EVL teardown on the hardware evl_en bit. When reset clears the bit to 0, the function exits before freeing idxd->evl, causing the memory leak described in the root cause.
